findings.where: First screen, the nav: 'Profile', 'Articles and talks' and 'Blog' (desktop top right, phone under the lockup)
findings.fault: All three nav items go to the same place, the article specimen (#article). 'Profile' promises Mark's background but opens a blog post, and 'Articles and talks' and 'Blog' can't be told apart by where they lead. Clicking the nav shows the visitor three labels for one destination, and one of the labels is wrong.
findings.who_objects: A development-bank officer checking who Mark is before writing to him would click 'Profile' and land in the middle of a PPP-law article with no profile in sight. The founder, judging the first screen as a visitor sees it, would hit the same dead end.

findings.where: Article specimen, the lecture row 'Streamlining the PPP Process: Meeting the ‘Abundance’ Challenge' with its blue download arrow and 'PDF'
findings.fault: The row promises a PDF download with a download arrow and the label 'PDF', but the link only jumps to #article on the same page, so the download does nothing. The row is the one sample of the PDF list the research calls the product, and as built it is a dead action.
findings.who_objects: A visitor who wants Mark's lecture to read offline or forward to colleagues clicks 'PDF', gets no file, and is moved to the top of the article they were already reading.

findings.where: Article specimen, the numbers 1–3 of the 'chapter topics' list
findings.fault: The list numbers are set in the house blue, which the page keeps for links. The specimen's own note says 'blue only where something can be clicked', but these numbers are static, so blue stops meaning one thing on the article page.
findings.who_objects: A reader scanning the article for links, such as Angélique checking her pages or a visitor looking for sources, sees blue numbers that look clickable and do nothing. Over time this weakens the one cue that tells a link from plain text in the article.

findings.where: First screen header, the name 'Mark M. Moseley' beside the linked MMM Infra mark
findings.fault: Mark's name, which leads the lockup at equal weight with the logo, does nothing when clicked, while the logo beside it links home. The top-left identity is normally one home link, and here half of it is dead.
findings.who_objects: A visitor deep in an article who clicks Mark's name to get back to the home page gets no response. They have to find the mark instead, and the name is the part the brief says should lead.

findings.where: Motion sketch, 'Replay the opening' (and the blue underlined email address in the footer)
findings.fault: 'Replay the opening' is a button that replays the animation on this page, but it is styled exactly like the page's links: blue text with an underline. The same look therefore means both 'go somewhere' (the footer mailto) and 'do something here' (replay).
findings.who_objects: The founder, or anyone reviewing the motion, can't tell whether it will play the opening in place or take them away from the page. It is low stakes, but the look stands for two functions.
